report.headline: REDUCE-IT succeeded with a 25% relative risk reduction (HR 0.75, p<0.001) in 8,179 high-risk patients on statins with residual hypertriglyceridemia after 4.9 years, substantially exceeding the 9.7% RRR predicted from non-HDL-C lowering alone.
report.summary: REDUCE-IT met its primary composite endpoint (CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularization, unstable angina) with HR 0.75 (25% RRR, p<0.001) in 8,179 patients followed for a median of 4.9 years. The observed benefit is 2.5-fold larger than the calculator's prediction of 9.7% RRR (HR 0.903) based solely on non-HDL-C reduction (-13.6%). Multiple pleiotropic effects were documented in phase 3 trials: hsCRP -22%, Lp-PLA2 -19%, Ox-LDL -13%, triglycerides -21.5%, apoB -9.3%, and EVAPORATE showed low-attenuation plaque reduction. JELIS (18,645 patients, HR 0.81) supports EPA benefit beyond lipid lowering. Safety in MARINE and ANCHOR was similar to placebo. The trial is rated success_with_caveats (mechanism exceeds lipid pathway) and robust_success (large effect, adequate power, consistent replication) with high confidence.
key_evidence: HR 0.75 (25% RRR, p<0.001) from REDUCE-IT Cardiovascular Outcomes Study of Vascepa (icosapent ethyl) Capsules Met Primary Endpoint

Other EPA/DHA cardiovascular outcome trials (STRENGTH, OMEMI) and triglyceride-lowering agents with distinct mechanisms (pemafibrate, volanesorsen) will clarify whether the effect is specific to icosapent ethyl or a broader class effect.

While triglyceride lowering via apoB is genetically causal, no single target with genetic support for CAD is established for EPA.

mechanism.notes: Biomarker changes from pooled ANCHOR+MARINE phase 3 (pmid:22819432) at 4 g/day on statin, 12 weeks, placebo-adjusted. ANCHOR enrolled TG 200-499 mg/dL on statin; MARINE enrolled TG ≥500 mg/dL (statin not required). REDUCE-IT enrolled TG 150-499 mg/dL on statin; pooled estimate may not perfectly represent REDUCE-IT population. Non-HDL-C baseline approximated as LDL-C + TG/5 (Friedewald) from REDUCE-IT announcement values (LDL-C 75 mg/dL, TG 216 mg/dL) = 118.2 mg/dL = 3.05 mmol/L; not a direct measurement. Calculator model uses lipid pathways only (non-HDL-C basis for triglyceride-lowering drug); does not capture pleiotropic effects: hsCRP -22%, Lp-PLA2 -19%, oxLDL -13% (ANCHOR 4g, f_4d961d0c0f4add), anti-platelet, membrane EPA incorporation, specialized pro-resolving mediators. These may explain the observed HR 0.75 vs calculator prediction.

issues.issue: Calculator assumes non-HDL-C baseline of 2.6 mmol/L ('assumed 2.6' in assumptions) without a verified source. REDUCE-IT announcement gives LDL-C 75 mg/dL (1.94 mmol/L) and TG 216 mg/dL but not non-HDL-C directly.
issues.request: Search for REDUCE-IT baseline non-HDL-C in announcement or protocol (ctgov:NCT01492361). If unavailable, document the assumption explicitly and test sensitivity (e.g., non-HDL-C ≈ LDL-C + TG/5 in mg/dL ≈ 75 + 43 = 118 mg/dL ≈ 3.05 mmol/L).

issues.issue: Biomarker changes come from pooled phase 3 (ANCHOR+MARINE) at 4 g/day on statin, 12 weeks. ANCHOR enrolled TG 200-499 mg/dL on statin; MARINE enrolled TG ≥500 mg/dL (statin not required). REDUCE-IT enrolled TG 150-499 mg/dL on statin. The pooled estimate may not perfectly represent the REDUCE-IT population.
issues.request: Check if ANCHOR alone (TG 200-499 on statin) provides a closer match to REDUCE-IT. ANCHOR 4 g/day LDL-C change -16.3% (f_76b71edbb1a31a), TG -27.9% (f_fc3b184cab3d68), non-HDL-C not directly given but can be derived. Consider using ANCHOR-only values as a sensitivity analysis.

issues.issue: Calculator lacks a pathway model for EPA's pleiotropic effects (anti-inflammatory: hsCRP -22%, Lp-PLA2 -19%; plaque stabilization: oxLDL -13% in ANCHOR; anti-platelet; membrane incorporation). The 'non-HDL-C (triglyceride-lowering drug)' basis captures only lipid-mediated effects.
issues.request: Document that the calculator's model is limited to lipid pathways. The departure_from_calculator correctly identifies this. No input change needed, but ensure the hypothesis 'insufficient_data' cites the missing mediators (EPA/AA ratio, SPMs, platelet reactivity) with fact references if available.

issues.issue: Hypothesis 'biomarker_not_causal' references a 'reference table' for genetics evidence (TG via apoB causal=yes, TG alone causal=uncertain) that is not in verified facts.
issues.request: Either add the genetics reference table as a verified fact or remove the parenthetical claim and cite only the calculator's target_genetics='uncertain' input.

issues.issue: Calculator uses LDL-C baseline 1.94 mmol/L (75 mg/dL) from REDUCE-IT announcement, but phase 3 trials had higher baselines (MARINE ~100-130 mg/dL, ANCHOR ~100 mg/dL, JELIS 4.7 mmol/L). The lower baseline in REDUCE-IT (statin-treated) reduces the absolute LDL-C/non-HDL-C change in mmol/L, which the calculator accounts for via baseline input.
issues.request: Confirm the 75 mg/dL LDL-C baseline is correct for REDUCE-IT (f_70643c5360e8cf confirmed). No change needed.

issues.issue: Time_factor of 0.988 for 4.9 years follow-up assumes constant hazard reduction over time. EPA's pleiotropic effects (plaque stabilization) may have a different time course than lipid lowering.
issues.request: Note as a caveat in hypotheses; no input change required.

issues.issue: The 'off_target_harm' hypothesis includes a 'for' claim stating 'REDUCE-IT reported increased atrial fibrillation and bleeding' with empty refs ([]). This claim has no support in the verified facts, which only contain MARINE/ANCHOR safety data (similar to placebo). In an evidence-gated system, claims without verified fact references must be removed or supported.
issues.request: Remove the unsupported atrial fibrillation/bleeding claim from the 'off_target_harm' hypothesis 'for' section, or add a verified fact reference from REDUCE-IT safety data if available.

issues.issue: non-HDL-C baseline in calculator inputs (3.05 mmol/L) is approximated from REDUCE-IT announcement LDL-C (75 mg/dL) + TG/5 (216/5=43.2 mg/dL) rather than directly measured. The method field notes this, but the approximation introduces uncertainty in the ldl_equivalent_mmol calculation (0.415 mmol/L).
issues.request: Note the approximation in calculator assumptions; consider sensitivity analysis using a range of plausible non-HDL-C baselines (e.g., 2.9-3.2 mmol/L) to assess impact on expected_hr.

issues.issue: Calculator pathway selection defaulted to non-HDL-C ('triglyceride-lowering drug') because pathway=null and no TG pathway exists in the model. The intended_biomarker is 'triglycerides' but the calculator cannot model TG-mediated risk reduction. This is a known calculator limitation, not an input error, but it affects interpretation of the 'narrow_success' category.
issues.request: Document in calculator assumptions that TG pathway is not modeled; the non-HDL-C basis is a proxy for atherogenic particle reduction.
